_comment: English bodies for open-interpreter (framework). Mechanism per C0-1..6. No extraSections in source; sections/sectionTitles omitted. providers not rendered — not included.

axes.model_access: Positioned as "a coding agent for open models" (official repo description and site title agree, naming open-weight models like Kimi K3 / GLM 5.3); open weights run locally + a terminal agent is its combined narrative.
axes.runtime: **A coding agent that runs in your terminal** (CLI form): the agent executes code/commands on your machine. GitHub openinterpreter/openinterpreter 68,746 stars, last push 2026-10-11 (API verified); releases follow the rust-v* line (rust-v0.0.56, 2026-10-07) — a Rust rewrite line on record.
axes.local_files: Local execution is the product itself: code and commands run directly on your machine, the working directory is your filesystem; there is no "runs for you in the cloud" hosted surface (no official hosted line found).
axes.background: **Resident in your terminal session**, looping execute-observe-continue per task; it is not a library-form base but a ready-to-use terminal agent (a different form factor from the SDK/framework entries).
axes.tools: Code execution / file / command tool surfaces are the core capability; MCP support status not itemized (the official docs have a terminal guide, details unchecked).
axes.context: Conversational context advances task by task (details not itemized); on the open-model side the context window depends on the local model you choose.
axes.permissions: **The permission surface is the selection crux**: the agent executes code and commands on your machine — the permission boundary of a local-execution agent must be defended by you (sandbox / least privilege / approval flows are operational duties, not a default safety net from the framework).
axes.fit: Fits: open-weight models + a local terminal coding agent, wanting execution on your own machine, followers of the Rust rewrite line. Does not fit: wanting cloud-hosted execution, enterprise control surfaces, or treating "local execution" as default-safe.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/framework/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/framework/_protocol.md).
